newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS TO STICK WITH BUNDS DESPITE SCANDALS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS TO STICK WITH BUNDS DESPITE SCANDALS.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds are unlikely to underperform Bunds in the weeks ahead, despite several potentially explosive scandals looming over the market, and could be heading for higher regions, traders said on Tuesday.
"We could see some good weeks in OLOs," said Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank. "I don't expect us to underperform Bunds and leave the normal range (for the OLO/Bund yield spread)," he said.
At 1520 GMT, the benchmark 2007 OLO was yielding 5.79 percent, unchanged from Monday's close, after earlier dipping to 5.78 percent. The spread over Bunds was seven basis points.
The spread was eight basis points late on Monday.
Fieremans said he believed it would continue to hover between zero and 10.
Fieremans said players were showing interest in the market but appeared to be waiting for U.S. Treasuries to edge lower before stepping in again.
Traders said the exchange auction was again a non-event with a modest 15.25 billion francs exchanged.
"It's not really a major success," Fieremans said. "Like last time," he added.
The two-day U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting, which kicked off today, was another event unlikely to stir any excitement.
"Nothing should be expected from it," Fieremans said.

Traders said the judicial investigation into Belgium's French-speaking socialist party (PS) and the likely lifting of the parliamentary immunity of the party's former president to allow him to be questioned over PS bribery allegations, was largely ignored, traders said.
They said that the government would act swiftly, if necessary, to reshuffle the government to avoid early elections.
"Elections would be the catastrophe scenario for the traditional parties which they will definitely try to avoid," he said.
